page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.ce4.xlarge is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features 4 dedicated physical cores on an Intel Xeon E5-2667 v4 processor running at a base frequency of 3.2 GHz. The instance is configured with 32.0 GB of x86_64 system memory, yielding a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core. It does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, relying instead on network-attached storage options. Network connectivity is rated at a baseline bandwidth of 2 Gbps.

Performance benchmarks indicate that the ecs.ce4.xlarge sits primarily in the lower tiers for compute-heavy and memory-bandwidth-intensive tasks. In stress-ng and Geekbench multi-core testing, the instance scores in the bottom 25%, reflecting its older Intel Xeon architecture. Memory bandwidth tests show a read-only large block transfer rate of 22.44 GB/sec and a write rate of 14.99 GB/sec. However, single-threaded operations perform relatively better, with gzip compression and Geekbench single-core scores reaching average tiers. Redis SET operations achieve 3.36 million operations per second, and static web serving throughput is measured at 4.28 GB/sec.

Given its older processor architecture and modest benchmark results, the ecs.ce4.xlarge offers a cost-efficient entry point for memory-intensive workloads that do not require high-performance compute. The high memory density makes it suitable for hosting medium-sized databases, caching layers like Redis, or running memory-bound enterprise applications. It is less suited for high-performance computing, large-scale LLM inference, or heavy multi-threaded compilation tasks due to its lower multi-core efficiency.
